source_hypothesis.claim_before_holdout: A local split that separates a stated mechanism from its consequence may reduce ZeroGPT and Scribbr scores on strict scientific prose, but it has not transferred across detector families or texts.

services.rationale: ZeroGPT and Scribbr have repeatable guest paths and belong to different registry groups. Sapling requires human controls because prior scientific and technical controls produced severe false positives.

procedure: Regenerate every candidate from the pinned original and exact replacement plan.
Reject candidates that fail fidelity, explicit C2, or style-distance screening before live scanning.
Scan each human control and AI baseline three times in each primary service.
Screen each quality-passing candidate once in each primary service.
Repeat H1 to n=3 only when its first result improves beyond the observed baseline noise in both primary services; otherwise retain it as screening-only.
Use Sapling only as a diagnostic cross-family observation with its paired human control.
Bind every score to the complete post-terminal visible-text SHA-256.
Do not create or alter holdout candidates in response to their detector scores.

per_sample: H1 lowers the displayed score beyond baseline repeat noise in both primary services.
H1 does not regress any observed independent detector group by more than 5 percentage points.
All claim, number, modality, causality, genre, C2, and source-style constraints remain satisfied.
confirmatory_success.rule_admission: Passing this two-sample holdout is necessary but not sufficient: the global protocol still requires calibration evidence on at least four texts before production integration.

failure_policy: A saturated or already-zero baseline is not counted as confirmatory success.
A blocked service is reported as blocked and never assigned an inferred score.
A quality-rejected candidate cannot support transfer even if a detector score falls.
If H1 fails either holdout sample, the sentence-split factor remains unadmitted.
